cards.hypothesis: Inter-subject variability in autonomic nervous system baseline tone causes systematic miscalibration of conformal prediction intervals when a single global calibration set is used across subjects.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Subjects with high resting sympathetic tone exhibit wider heart rate variability (HRV) distributions during calibration, but conformal prediction uses a fixed quantile threshold from pooled data, leading to under-coverage for high-tone subjects and over-coverage for low-tone subjects.
cards.causal_path: High resting sympathetic tone -> increased HRV dispersion in calibration segment -> pooled quantile threshold too narrow for this subject -> prediction intervals too narrow -> coverage drops below nominal
control_variables: stratify calibration by LF/HF ratio tertiles
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is driven by sensor noise differences across subjects rather than physiological differences.
cards.rival_prediction: Subjects with noisier signals (lower SNR) show worse coverage regardless of autonomic tone.
cards.distinguishing_test: Regress coverage error on both LF/HF ratio and signal SNR; if LF/HF remains significant after controlling for SNR, H1 is supported over rival.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior work shows LF/HF ratio explains 15-25% of HRV variance; expect coverage deviation of 5-10% per SD of LF/HF.
minimum_data_needed: ECG recordings from >=30 subjects with >=10 min resting baseline each
simultaneous ECG and impedance cardiography for LF/HF computation
ground truth labels for prediction target (e.g., arrhythmia events)
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage rate negatively correlates with subject resting LF/HF ratio when using pooled calibration (r < -0.3).
cards.failure_condition: No significant correlation between LF/HF ratio and coverage error after SNR adjustment (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage_error ~ LF_HF_ratio + SNR + (1|subject); test LF_HF_ratio coefficient.
cards.falsification_test: Perform subject-specific calibration (separate quantile per subject); if coverage stabilizes across LF/HF strata, the pooled-calibration mechanism is confirmed as the cause.

cards.hypothesis: Motion artifact contamination varies systematically across physiological signal segments, causing non-exchangeability between calibration and test segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Segments with high motion artifact (measured by accelerometer variance) have distorted morphological features used by the non-conformity score, shifting the score distribution relative to clean calibration segments.
cards.causal_path: High motion artifact -> increased accelerometer variance -> distorted ECG morphology -> non-conformity score distribution shift -> conformal quantile from clean calibration misestimates test uncertainty -> coverage failure
control_variables: stratify segments by accelerometer variance quartiles
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage drops during motion because physiological state genuinely changes (e.g., stress), not because of measurement artifact.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage correlates with physiological stress markers (cortisol, skin conductance) but not with accelerometer variance after controlling for stress.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage in high-motion/low-stress (e.g., rhythmic exercise) vs. low-motion/high-stress (e.g., mental arithmetic) segments; H2 predicts worse coverage in former, rival in latter.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Motion artifacts can increase ECG amplitude variance by 300-500%; expect coverage drops of 15-30% in high-artifact segments.
minimum_data_needed: Synchronized ECG and triaxial accelerometer data
Segment-level artifact annotations or automated quality indices
>=50 segments spanning low to high motion
Ground truth for prediction target in each segment
cards.testable_prediction: Segment coverage rate decreases monotonically with accelerometer variance (Spearman rho < -0.5).
cards.failure_condition: No monotonic relationship between accelerometer variance and coverage error (p > 0.05 for trend test).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Quantile regression of coverage on accelerometer variance; test for negative slope at 0.5 quantile.
cards.falsification_test: Apply motion-artifact removal (e.g., adaptive filtering) to high-artifact segments; if coverage recovers to nominal, artifact is the causal mechanism.

cards.hypothesis: Circadian-driven non-stationarity in physiological signal statistics violates the exchangeability assumption between calibration (daytime) and test (nighttime) segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Core body temperature and autonomic balance shift across circadian phases, altering the marginal distribution of the prediction target (e.g., QT interval) and the non-conformity scores, making daytime calibration invalid for nighttime segments.
cards.causal_path: Circadian phase (melatonin onset) -> core temperature drop + parasympathetic dominance -> QT interval prolongation and reduced variability -> non-conformity score distribution shifts left -> daytime calibration quantile too conservative -> over-coverage at night
control_variables: stratify calibration by circadian phase bins
include core temperature as covariate in non-conformity score
cards.rival_explanation: Nighttime coverage changes are due to sleep-stage-specific physiology, not circadian phase per se.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage varies by sleep stage (NREM vs REM) within the same circadian phase, not by circadian phase alone.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage in NREM sleep at two different circadian phases (e.g., early vs late night); H3 predicts difference, rival predicts none.
cards.effect_size_rationale: QT interval varies ~30-50ms across circadian cycle; expect 5-15% coverage deviation if calibration ignores phase.
minimum_data_needed: 24+ hour continuous ECG with core temperature monitoring
Dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO) markers or validated proxy
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage error shows a significant sinusoidal pattern across circadian phase (cosinor analysis p < 0.01).
cards.failure_condition: Cosinor analysis shows no significant circadian rhythm in coverage error (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Cosinor regression: coverage_error ~ cos(2π*phase/24) + sin(2π*phase/24) + (1|subject); test amplitude > 0.
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate conformal predictor separately for each 4-hour circadian bin; if coverage stabilizes across phases, non-stationarity is confirmed as cause.

cards.hypothesis: Temporal concept drift in the relationship between physiological features and the prediction target causes conformal prediction intervals to become miscalibrated as recording duration increases.
cards.proposed_mechanism: The conditional distribution P(Y|X) shifts gradually over hours due to factors like electrode impedance changes, skin hydration, or slow physiological adaptation, violating the i.i.d. assumption underlying split conformal prediction.
cards.causal_path: Recording duration -> electrode impedance drift / skin hydration change -> feature distribution shift (e.g., R-peak amplitude) -> P(Y|X) changes -> non-conformity scores from early calibration no longer valid for late test -> coverage decays with time
control_variables: use online conformal prediction with forgetting factor
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage decay is due to increasing subject fatigue/stress over time, not sensor drift.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage correlates with subjective fatigue ratings or cortisol, not with electrode impedance.
cards.distinguishing_test: In a controlled lab study with impedance monitoring, regress coverage error on both elapsed time and impedance; H4 predicts impedance mediates the time effect.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Electrode impedance typically drifts 10-20% over 24h; expect 2-5% coverage decay per 8 hours if uncorrected.
minimum_data_needed: Long-duration ECG (>=12h) with continuous electrode impedance logging
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage rate declines linearly with recording elapsed time (slope < -0.5% per hour).
cards.failure_condition: No significant linear trend in coverage over time (p > 0.05 for slope).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage ~ elapsed_hours + (elapsed_hours|subject); test fixed effect slope.
cards.falsification_test: Implement sliding-window recalibration (e.g., every 30 min); if coverage stabilizes, temporal drift is confirmed as mechanism.

cards.hypothesis: Inconsistent ground truth labeling across annotators or algorithms for different physiological segments introduces label noise that breaks conformal prediction's coverage guarantee.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Segments with ambiguous morphology (e.g., low-amplitude T-waves) receive noisier labels; the non-conformity score learns to predict the noisy label distribution, but coverage is evaluated against a different (consensus) ground truth, causing miscalibration.
cards.causal_path: Ambiguous segment morphology -> high inter-annotator disagreement (low Fleiss kappa) -> noisy training labels -> non-conformity score fits label noise -> prediction intervals reflect label variance not true uncertainty -> coverage fails on consensus labels
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage fails on ambiguous segments because the prediction task is inherently harder, not because of label noise.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage correlates with morphology ambiguity even when using perfect simulated labels (no label noise).
cards.distinguishing_test: Simulate perfect labels from a known generative model; if coverage still drops on ambiguous segments, rival wins. If coverage recovers, H5 wins.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Inter-annotator kappa for ECG segments ranges 0.6-0.9; expect coverage gap of 5-15% between high/low kappa segments.
minimum_data_needed: ECG segments with >=3 independent expert annotations each
Morphology ambiguity metrics (e.g., T-wave amplitude SNR)
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage error negatively correlates with inter-annotator Fleiss kappa (rho < -0.4).
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between kappa and coverage error (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Spearman correlation between segment kappa and coverage error; bootstrap CI for rho.
cards.falsification_test: Train conformal predictor on consensus labels only; if coverage stabilizes across kappa strata, label noise was the mechanism.

cards.hypothesis: Improper stratification during calibration—ignoring known physiological state changes (e.g., sleep stages)—causes conformal prediction to produce miscalibrated intervals for minority states.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Calibration set pools all sleep stages, but non-conformity score distributions differ markedly between NREM (stable) and REM (variable) sleep; the pooled quantile is dominated by abundant NREM data, yielding under-coverage for REM segments.
cards.causal_path: Sleep stage (REM vs NREM) -> different HRV dynamics -> different non-conformity score distributions -> pooled calibration quantile biased toward NREM -> REM segments get intervals too narrow -> REM coverage < nominal
cards.rival_explanation: REM coverage fails because REM segments are shorter, giving fewer samples for non-conformity estimation, not because of distributional shift.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage correlates with segment duration, not sleep stage, when duration is controlled.
cards.distinguishing_test: Match NREM and REM segments by duration; compare coverage. H6 predicts REM still worse; rival predicts equal.
cards.effect_size_rationale: REM HRV variance can be 2-3x NREM; expect 15-25% coverage gap if pooling ignores stage.
minimum_data_needed: Ground truth for prediction target per epoch
cards.testable_prediction: REM segment coverage is at least 15 percentage points lower than NREM coverage under pooled calibration.
cards.failure_condition: REM and NREM coverage difference < 5% (p > 0.05 for difference).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Paired t-test (within-subject) of REM vs NREM coverage; mixed model with stage as fixed effect.
cards.falsification_test: Apply sleep-stage-stratified conformal prediction; if REM coverage reaches nominal, improper stratification was the cause.

cards.hypothesis: Temporal autocorrelation in physiological signals violates the exchangeability assumption, causing conformal prediction to underestimate uncertainty in highly autocorrelated segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: High autocorrelation (e.g., during stable NREM sleep) reduces the effective sample size of the calibration set; the conformal quantile is computed assuming n independent samples but effective n is much smaller, yielding overconfident intervals.
cards.causal_path: High signal autocorrelation (AR1 coefficient) -> reduced effective sample size in calibration -> conformal quantile too narrow (underestimates sampling variability) -> prediction intervals too narrow -> coverage below nominal
control_variables: use time-series conformal prediction (e.g., conformalized quantile regression with dependent data)
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage drops in high-autocorrelation segments because physiological state is more predictable, so the model is overconfident correctly, not due to exchangeability violation.
cards.rival_prediction: Prediction interval width appropriately narrows in high-autocorrelation segments; coverage failure is due to model misspecification, not quantile miscalibration.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare conformal intervals vs. oracle intervals (from known generative model) in high-autocorrelation segments; H7 predicts conformal intervals narrower than oracle, rival predicts similar.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Effective n can drop to 10-20% of nominal n for AR1=0.8; expect 5-15% coverage deficit.
minimum_data_needed: Long stationary ECG segments (>=30 min) with varying autocorrelation
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage error negatively correlates with AR1 coefficient (rho < -0.3).
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between AR1 and coverage error (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear regression: coverage_error ~ AR1_coef + segment_length + HR_mean; test AR1_coef.
cards.falsification_test: Use block bootstrap (block size = decorrelation time) to compute calibration quantile; if coverage recovers, exchangeability violation was the mechanism.

cards.hypothesis: Varying signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) across segments causes heteroscedastic non-conformity scores, which a single global conformal quantile cannot accommodate.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Low-SNR segments (e.g., due to poor electrode contact) produce noisier features, inflating non-conformity scores; the global quantile is pulled toward high-SNR segments, yielding under-coverage for low-SNR segments and over-coverage for high-SNR segments.
cards.causal_path: Low electrode contact quality -> low ECG SNR -> high feature noise -> inflated non-conformity scores -> global quantile dominated by high-SNR majority -> low-SNR segments get intervals too narrow -> coverage drops
cards.rival_explanation: Low-SNR segments have genuinely higher physiological variability, not just measurement noise.
cards.rival_prediction: After denoising (e.g., wavelet filtering), coverage gap between high/low SNR segments persists.
cards.distinguishing_test: Apply aggressive denoising to low-SNR segments; if coverage gap closes, H8 (measurement noise) wins; if gap persists, rival (physiological variability) wins.
cards.effect_size_rationale: SNR can vary 20-40 dB across segments; expect 20-40% coverage gap between best/worst SNR quartiles.
minimum_data_needed: ECG with electrode impedance monitoring per segment
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage rate increases monotonically with ECG SNR (Spearman rho > 0.5).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Quantile regression of coverage on SNR; test positive slope.
cards.falsification_test: Stratify calibration by SNR quartile; if coverage equalizes across strata, heteroscedasticity was the mechanism.

cards.hypothesis: Abrupt physiological state transitions (e.g., sleep onset, stress onset) create transient non-stationarities where calibration data from the prior state misrepresents the new state's uncertainty.
cards.proposed_mechanism: At state boundaries (e.g., wake-to-sleep transition), the non-conformity score distribution shifts rapidly; calibration data from the previous state yields quantiles mismatched to the new state, causing temporary coverage collapse until sufficient new-state data accumulates.
cards.causal_path: Physiological state transition (e.g., sleep onset) -> abrupt change in HRV dynamics -> non-conformity score distribution shift -> calibration quantile from pre-transition state invalid -> coverage drops transiently -> recovers as new-state calibration accumulates
control_variables: online conformal prediction with change-point detection
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage drops at transitions because the prediction model itself performs poorly on transitional physiology, not because of conformal calibration lag.
cards.rival_prediction: Point prediction error (MAE) spikes at transitions; conformal intervals widen appropriately but model bias causes misses.
cards.distinguishing_test: Decompose coverage failure into interval width vs. centering: H7 predicts intervals too narrow (width issue); rival predicts intervals centered wrong (bias issue).
cards.effect_size_rationale: Transitions last 2-10 min; expect 10-30% coverage drop in first 5 min post-transition if calibration lags.
minimum_data_needed: Continuous ECG with annotated state transitions (sleep staging, stress markers)
Transition detection algorithm or manual annotations
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage in first 5 min post-transition is at least 15% lower than steady-state coverage.
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage drop in post-transition window vs. steady state (p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Mixed model: coverage ~ time_since_transition (spline) + (1|subject); test non-zero dip at t=0-5min.
cards.falsification_test: Reset calibration at each detected transition; if transient coverage drop disappears, calibration lag was the mechanism.

cards.hypothesis: The choice of non-conformity score function interacts with segment-specific physiological characteristics, causing miscalibration when a single score function is used across heterogeneous segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: A non-conformity score based on residual magnitude (|y - ŷ|) assumes homoscedastic errors, but physiological segments exhibit state-dependent heteroscedasticity (e.g., higher variability during REM); the score function fails to normalize for this, making the quantile invalid for high-variability segments.
cards.causal_path: Physiological state (e.g., REM) -> increased conditional variance of target -> residual magnitude non-conformity score conflates aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty -> quantile reflects average variance not state-specific variance -> high-variance segments under-covered
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage fails because the base predictor (ŷ) is biased in certain states, not because of the non-conformity score choice.
cards.rival_prediction: Predictor bias (mean residual) correlates with coverage error; switching to a better predictor fixes coverage without changing non-conformity score.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage using residual magnitude vs. normalized residual (residual/predicted_std) as non-conformity score; H10 predicts normalized score equalizes coverage across states without changing predictor.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Conditional variance can vary 3-5x across sleep stages; expect 10-20% coverage gap with naive score, <5% with normalized.
minimum_data_needed: >=50 segments per state for quantile estimation
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage gap between high-variance and low-variance states is >15% with residual magnitude score but <5% with normalized score.
cards.failure_condition: Normalized score does not reduce coverage gap significantly (gap reduction < 50%, p > 0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Paired comparison of coverage gaps (high-variance state minus low-variance state) between two non-conformity scores; Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
cards.falsification_test: Use a heteroscedasticity-aware conformal method (e.g., CQR with predicted quantiles); if coverage stabilizes, score function mismatch was the mechanism.
